XX Global Open Synchronous Championship
Season 2022–2023
Leg III (04.11 – 13.11.2022)


Notes for the reader:



Please familiarize yourself with the question pack set before the game.



Words in capital letters (e.g., X, FIRST, IT, DO THIS) should be emphasized when reading out loud. After reading the answer, you should also read out other accepted answers and the commentary to the question. Reading out the name(s) of the author(s) is advisable but not necessary.



Additional notes for the reader are placed in square brackets before some of the questions. You must not read them out loud.



Phonetic transcriptions of selected words (in square brackets) are put within the text of some questions for the reader’s convenience.



Handouts for questions 11 and 35 are placed before the text of the questions. Please give the teams some time to familiarise themselves with the handouts, but do not read them out loud.



Good luck!



Block 1


Edited by Yulia Didbaridze [did-bah-RID-zeh]



The editor thanks the following people for testing the questions: Sergei Grigoriev [gree-GOR-yeff], Natalia Komar, Yuri Motkin, Maxim Merzlyakov [mers-lyah-KOFF], Sergei Terentyev [te-RENT-yeff], Andrei & Anastasia Tsepaev [tse-PIE-eff], and the teams «Absolutnoe menshinstvo» [abso-LUTE-noh-yeh men-shins-TVOH], «Guliay rvanina» [goo-LYAY rvah-NEE-nah] and «Krainiaya sbornaya» [CRY-nya-yuh ZBORE-nah-yuh]



Question 1.
Initially, the creators of Netflix wanted to use the bleating of a goat, which would be a reference to THIS. Identify THIS using a palindrome.

Answer: the MGM opening logo [accept any answers that mention MGM]
Comment: Instead of the now-iconic «tu-dum» sound, episodes could have been introduced by the bleating of a goat, which would be a reference to the MGM lion’s roar. However, later the Netflix founders said that they were happy to have dropped this idea.

Source: https://www.20k.org/episodes/netflix
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 2.
In the mid-19th century, a rich heir Roger Tichborne was travelling on a ship that disappeared. Later, the lack of an anchor helped Tichborne’s family prove in court that it was not Roger, who had apparently survived, but actually an impostor. It is believed that this court case popularised… WHAT?

Answer: tattoos [acceptable answer: tattoo]
Comment: Roger followed the sailors’ custom and got a tattoo with a heart and an anchor. The impostor did not have such a tattoo. After that case tattoos became widespread among the general populace.

Sources:
1. https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/law-and-social-justice/news/articles/how-tattoos-became-fashionable-in-victorian-england/
2. https://collections.countway.harvard.edu/onview/items/show/13074
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 3.
Marshall Islands are a winding chain of atolls and islands with curved coastlines. Local seafarers used to say that the best method to find one’s way was using THEM, and in dangerous situations would lie down on the canoe’s floor in order to determine which island is the nearest. What are THEY?

Answer: waves
Comment: Such natural conditions are conducive to the emergence of unique wave patterns around each island, and local navigators could determine their position by these patterns.

Sources:
1. https://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/science-and-tradition-are-resurrecting-lost-art-wave-piloting-180958005/
2. https://skifiabook.ru/store/psihologiya-medicina/item_112.html
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 4.
In the latter half of the 19th century, French intellectuals, appalled by the prevalence of criminals in research, founded the Society of Mutual Improvement. In order to help with later studies, the members would write an essay about their character upon joining the Society. Which word in the Society’s name did we substitute?

Answer: autopsy [accepted answer: post-mortem]
Comment: The scientists were appalled by the fact that in medicine all important conclusions were based on autopsies of criminals and proposed to solve this issue with their own efforts.

Source: https://mindhacks.com/2014/02/21/the-society-of-mutual-autopsy/
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 5.
In order to draw attention to a widespread social evil, a certain company launched a line of alcoholic beverages with names such as Rachel, Carol, and Irene. Which ADJECTIVE did we omit in the text of this question several times?

Answer: Bloody
Comment: The line of beers called Bloody Women was intended to draw attention to the issue of domestic abuse. The name was based on the famous cocktail, the Bloody Mary.

Source: https://www.thedrinksbusiness.com/2021/11/female-hk-brewers-launch-beer-to-raise-awareness-on-domestic-abuse
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 6.
Dugu Xin [Doo-goo SHIN], a 6th-century Chinese official, held several positions at the same time and was active in all of them. The man who found X that used to belong to Dugu Xin, at first thought it was a gambling die. What is X?

Answer: seal of office [accept any answer that mentions a seal]
Comment: Dugu Xin worked with official papers and, for the sake of convenience, didn’t carry around many seals for each of his offices, but rather had them made into one, which had 26 faces.

Sources:
1. https://inf.news/en/collect/9f79b7d701cb62b8d04b23cd39299daf.html
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dugu_Xin
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 7.
Having learned about a visit by the higher-ups, some officials in a rural district of China handed out big white sacks to children. The sacks were to play the role of THIS. Who uses THIS in a common saying?

Answer: wolf
Comment: THIS stands for «a sheep’s clothing» or a sheep’s coat of wool. The children were to stand in the fields, wearing the white sacks, and look like sheep. This way the officials wanted to paint a picture of prosperity in their district.

Source: https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/chinas-xi-tells-grumbling-party-cadres-dont-talk-back/2015/12/27/a6b25d2c-a446-11e5-8318-bd8caed8c588_story.html
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 8.
A device developed by Leanne Wijnsma [Leh-AHN-neh VINE-smah], that warns about data leaks, needs to be filled up and then connected to a phone or a laptop. Its creator believes that this works faster than a sound signal, and compares data to X. What is X?

Answer: gas [accepted answers: methane, natural gas]
Comment: When there is a leak threat, the device starts emitting a pungent odour. Its creator was inspired by warning systems in cooking stoves, in which natural gas is mixed with an unpleasant smelling mercaptan to help people notice the leak.

Source: https://smellofdata.com/
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 9.
In the ancient Egyptian tale, The Doomed Prince, the main character receives a prophecy and then a house is built for him in the desert. However, he leaves that house and eventually meets his fate. It is thought that this tale influenced the fate of a certain captain. WHO was this captain?

Answer: James Hook [accepted answers: Captain Hook, Hook]
Comment: The protagonist is prophesied to die in a crocodile’s maw, so his parents try to send him away from danger. It has been proposed that the crocodile that pursues Captain Hook in Peter Pan, was inspired by this tale.

Source: https://arzamas.academy/mag/910-help
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 10.
In the opera Gould’s Wall, the protagonist wants to reach the same level of perfection as the great pianist Glenn Gould. The seats in the theatre hall are set at an angle for better comfort, and the performer must wear THIS on her feet while on stage. What is THIS?

Answer: [rock] climbing shoes
Comment: The creators of this opera wanted to literalize the metaphor about «reaching the pinnacle of accomplishment», so that throughout the performance the main character climbs a vertical wall in full climbing gear, and manages to sing all the while.

Sources:
1. https://tapestryopera.com/performances/goulds-wall/
2. https://www.thestar.com/entertainment/music/2022/07/29/the-opera-goulds-wall-has-the-soprano-climbing-an-18-metre-rock-wall.html
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 11.
Handout

(img 2022-2023_III_en_001.png)
A Slow Year is a videogame, in which the player needs to wait for a leaf to fall from a tree in autumn and look at fresh snow in winter. Each part of the game opens with THIS. You have been given THIS in a comic strip format. What is THIS?

Answer: haiku [accepted answer: hokku]
Comment: The game does not require any active input from the player and has a contemplative mood, which is enhanced by the instructions written as haiku. The author of this strip visualized a haiku through the proportions of the panels and the number of raindrops.

Sources:
1. https://kotaku.com/what-if-a-video-game-was-poetry-453104628
2. https://mattmadden.com/2013/06/20/haiku-comics/
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Question 12.
Each participant of a festival taking place in Colorado receives a t-shirt. In order to put the shirt on during a competition, they carefully strike and crease it first, while trying not to tear it off. The festival is dedicated to Bredo Morstuhl whose loving gransdon is an advocate of THIS. Name THIS using a word derived from Greek.

Answer: cryonics [accept cryopreservation and any other word with cryo-]
Comment: The t-shirts are frozen, just like the man to whom the festival is dedicated. The event also includes plunging in freezing cold water and bowling with a frozen turkey. This way, one dead old guy became a cause for celebration for many people.

Source: https://youtu.be/4MzGrNOqB5I
Author: Yulia Didbaridze

Block 2


Edited by: Yuri Razumov [RAH-zoom-off]



Questions tested by: Artyom Guletsky [goo-LETS-key], Andrei Zabavin [zah-BAH-vin], Irina Kolesnikova [caw-LESS-nick-oh-vuh], Eugene Mirotin [mee-RAW-tin], Vera Monina [MAW-nee-nuh].



Question 13.
The first edition of Johann Fichte’s [FICK-tay] first book was published without any mention of the author’s name, only stating the city where it was written. The book received wide acclaim, and then a famous individual had to make a statement. In Which city did Fichte write the book?

Answer: Koenigsberg [accepted answers: Kralovec, Kaliningrad]
Comment: A philosophical treatise written in Koenigsberg was immediately believed to be a new work by Kant (who lived there and had not published anything for a long time). However, the book got its reputation on merit, not only due to his presumed authorship, and when Kant made it clear that the author was not him, but Fichte, the latter was offered tenure at the Jena University.

Source: Andrea Wulf, Magnificent Rebels.
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 14.
Who knows where an arrow will land when it is shot from a bow? In a novel by Philip Jose Farmer, the Dokalians use the depiction of a bow and arrow as an analogue for THIS. What is THIS?

Answer: Question mark. [accepted answer: ?]
Comment: Until the arrow has hit its target, it can be seen as a symbol of uncertainty. Unlike the Dothraki in George Martin’s series, the Dokalians did not have a full-fledged artificial language. Curiously Philip Jose Farmer wrote this novel under the pseudonym Kilgore Trout, a fictional writer from Kurt Vonnegut’s books, so that some reviewers believed the book was by Vonnegut.

Source: Philip Jose Farmer, Venus on The Half-Shell.
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 15.
In a long historical novel by Anthony Burgess, a character notes that changes have affected not only the British royal family, but also Henry James, who stopped walking his X. Identify the X.

Answer: Dachshund. [accepted answers: Dachs, sausage dog, wiener dog]
Comment: After the outbreak of the First World War, the British royal dynasty dropped its German name Saxe-Coburg-Gotha and became the Windsors. In Britain, dachshunds were seen as German and featured heavily in propaganda (however, the stories about them being deliberately killed are a myth). The famous writer Henry James did indeed have a dachshund, named Max, but most probably he just stopped taking particularly long walks where he could be easily seen with the dog. James dedicated much of his time to Britain’s war effort (and even became a British citizen), and Max was 11 years old at that time, which is quite a lot for a dog.

Source: Anthony Burgess, Earthly Powers.
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 16.
Even seemingly identical objects can have different magnetic properties. In a system proposed by Martin Lauer, a sensor placed on THIS measures the magnetic profile directly underneath, and a specially prepared map enhances the GPS, increasing safety. What is THIS?

Answer: train. [accepted answers: locomotive, train engine]
Comment: GPS is not precise enough to distinguish between adjacent rail tracks, while tunnels interfere with satellite connection Even though all rails look identical, modern sensors are capable of identifying them by their magnetic profiles, which allows to make a precise map of the tracks and use it for safer and more efficient scheduling.

Sources:
1. https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2022/09/28/keeping-trains-apart-is-crucial-to-safety
2. https://www.itk-engineering.de/en/story/magnetic-railway-onboard-sensor/
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 17.
In 2007, a replica of a Phoenician ship was built in the Middle East that later proved capable of crossing the ocean. Today this replica is kept in a landlocked US state because in 2021 the ship was bought by THEM. Who are THEY?

Answer: Mormons [accepted answers: The Church of Latter-Day Saints, the Latter-Day Saints, the LDS Church]
Comment: The ship reached America under its own power. The researchers first demonstrated that a 5th century BCE Phoenician ship could plausibly sail along the African continent to the equator (a fact possibly mentioned by Herodotus), and then sailed from Tunisia to Florida. According to the Book of Mormon, a group of Israelites reached America soon after the fall of Jerusalem to the Babylonians, and so modern Mormons have an understandable interest in ancient ocean-going ships.

Sources:
1. https://web.archive.org/web/20220713100707/https://twitter.com/cwjones89/status/1547160424759451650
2. https://www.phoenicia.rocks/
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 18.
Many Ancient Roman epigrams had salacious subject matter and often contained insults. Having studied these and other ancient sources, 18th-century scholar Jean Astruc came to the correct conclusion that THIS appeared in Europe only in the late 15th century. What is THIS?

Answer: syphilis.
Comment: Many Roman epigrams openly describe sexual acts, and insulting verses would certainly have featured references to a disease like syphilis, had the Romans known it. However, neither satirists nor historians or the Bible mention such symptoms. Astruc collated this fact and the descriptions by 15th-century doctors concluding that syphilis first reached Europe as a result of Columbus’s voyages.

Sources:
1. The Cambridge Companion to Erotic Literature.
2. Jean Astruc, De Morbus Veneris (https://archive.org/details/b30531093_0002/page/66/mode/2up)
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 19.
An article describing the periodic necessity of THIS is illustrated with a picture of a spinning figure skater. Thawing and freezing glaciers are compared to the skater’s arms. Identify THIS, using two words exactly.

Answer: leap second.
Comment: When ice caps on mountain peaks thaw and freeze again, this affects the speed of the Earth’s rotation. In a similar way, but much more drastically, figure skaters can change the speed of their own rotation by adjusting the position of their arms. The inaccuracies in time measurements accumulate progressively, so that from time to time a leap second must be added to a year. Figure skaters are known to leap a lot.

Source: https://engineering.fb.com/2022/07/25/production-engineering/its-time-to-leave-the-leap-second-in-the-past/
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 20.
The only things the 5-year-old Samuel Seymour remembered from that evening were a tall man and another man leaping from a very high place. In 1956, then elderly Seymour took part in a TV show called I’ve Got a Secret. What was his secret?

Answer: He witnessed Lincoln’s assassination [accept all answers that mention Abraham Lincoln’s death].
Comment: Seymour’s family attended the performance of Our American Cousin, during which Abraham Lincoln was assassinated. Sam was shown where the President was seated (and Lincoln was famously 193 cm tall). Having shot Lincoln, John Wilkes Booth jumped from the box onto the stage and escaped; the boy mostly remembered the leap, and not the shots. In 1956, as the last surviving witness of the event, Seymour took part in a TV show.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_J._Seymour
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 21.
Contrary to conspiracy theories, global warming is a real issue. Research has shown that THESE THINGS can have different effects depending on weather and time of day, and now an enterprise called Satavia is developing schedules that would take this fact into account. What are THESE THINGS?

Answer: contrails [accepted answer: condensation trails, vapour trails].
Comment: On the one hand, contrails contain greenhouse gases, but on the other hand, they can reflect sunlight. Understanding which of the two effects is stronger in what conditions, can help build flight schedules that would mitigate the deleterious effects of flying planes. According to a popular conspiracy, contrails are formed when mind-control substances are dispersed from planes.

Source: https://medium.datadriveninvestor.com/reducing-contrails-by-rerouting-aircraft-957a95f51d67
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 22.
While watching a documentary about Liverpool FC, one finds that the Spaniard Pepe Reina and the Brazilian Lucas Leiva don’t need THIS, unlike the Liverpool-born Jamie Carragher. What is THIS?

Answer: subtitles [accepted answer: subs, captions].
Comment: Scouse accent is harder to understand than Brazilian or Spanish one. So the movie that was made for US viewers had subtitles only in scenes that feature Carragher.

Source: https://metro.co.uk/2012/10/12/jamie-carragher-given-subtitles-in-tv-documentary-being-liverpool-598968/
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 23.
In the 16th century Joachim du Bellay wrote that some of his contemporaries saw science and poetry as if they were holy relics, kept behind a glass. Du Bellay wrote a treatise defending THIS. Identify THIS.

Answer: the French language.
Comment: In the 16th century many still believed that both scientific works and works of poetry can be written only in Latin or Greek, which were as dead as saints’ relics (usually parts of their dead bodies). Du Bellay and other poets in La Pleiade group wrote in French.

Sources:
1. Walter Pater, The Renaissance: Studies in Art and Poetry. https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/2398/pg2398-images.html
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Défense_et_illustration_de_la_langue_française
Author: Yuri Razumov

Question 24.
Yellow-legged frogs live in mountain streams. To prepare captive-bred frogs for release, Talisin Hammond used THIS. Which surname is often associated with THIS?

Answer: Jacuzzi.
Comment: Swimming against the current is hard, and captive-bred frogs need to train for that. Water streams in a jacuzzi bath are like a treadmill for them.

Source: https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2022/06/01/the-health-giving-benefits-of-jacuzzis-for-frogs
Author: Yuri Razumov

Block 3


Edited by Alexei Sheredega [sherry-DEH-gah]



The editor thanks the following people for testing the questions: Yulia Archangelskaya [ar-KHANG-ell-sky-uh], Svetlana Alypova [ah-LIP-oh-vuh], Alexander Yermishkin [yerr-MISH-kin], Vitali Kunashko [coo-NAHSH-caw], Maxim Merzliakov [mers-lyah-KOFF], Evgenia Miller, Daniil Mordin, Polina Nasledskova [nass-LED-skaw-vuh], Artem Sapozhnikov [sah-PODGE-nick-off], Alexander Snovsky [SNOFF-ski], Elman Talybov [tah-LIB-off], Yana Khlustova [CLUE-stoh-vuh].



Question 25.
Leonard Mlodinov [MLAW-dee-noff] writes about a man who grew rich after he took notice of a barely discernible imbalance. In which South European city did this happen?

Answer: Monte Carlo [accepted answer: Monaco].
Comment: Joseph Jagger, a mechanical engineer, noticed that one roulette wheel favoured some numbers over the others and realized that these coincidences were not random and were due to a weight imbalance of the wheel. Jagger started betting on these exact numbers and won a substantial sum, until the wheel got changed. Monte Carlo is the biggest gambling centre of Europe.

Source: Леонард Млодинов. Совершенная случайность, стр. 132 [Leonard Mlodinov, Completely Accidentally]
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 26.
The playwright George Ade wrote about the life of the downtrodden in Chicago. Before the London premiere of one play by Ade, the spectators were given a kind of THIS. Identify THIS, using a word with a hyphen in it.

Answer: British-American dictionary [acceptable answers: American-British dictionary, or with «English» instead of «British»].
Comment: many words that had at the time become commonplace in America were unknown in Britain.

Sources:
1. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Ade
2. Rap Keyes. Hidden history of coined words
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 27.
In the middle of the last century, a group of officials was considering, among others, the designation «man-in-a-can», until someone thought of the story of Jason. Identify their final choice.

Answer: astronaut[s].
Comment: In 1958, NASA created a special group that had to devise a name for the future space explorers. Among the tongue-in-cheek options there was man-in-a-can, which sounded like «mannequin». But eventually someone saw the similarities with the quest for the Golden Fleece, and suggested a word that echoed «argonaut».

Sources:
1. http://www.collectspace.com/review/kcstoever/gamble-essay6.pdf
2. Loyd S. Swenson Jr., James M. Grimwood, Charles C. Alexander «This New Ocean: A History of Project Mercury»
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 28.
Let’s continue. The 1998 movie Meet Joe Black holds the unofficial record for the biggest number of viewers who bought the ticket but did not see the movie itself. The explanation is that the distributors didn’t see THIS as a potential problem. Identify THIS as precisely as possible.

Answer: trailer for Star Wars Episode 1: The Phantom Menace [accept all answers that mention a trailer or a promo roll for Star Wars, Star Wars Ep 1, Phantom Menace]
Comment: The fans were so excited for the restart of the saga, that they were ready to visit theaters only for the trailer and then leave before the 3-hour feature started. The Phantom Menace became something of a menace for the distributors too. And this question continued the space.

Sources:
1. decider.com/2018/11/13/star-wars-the-phantom-menace-trailer-meet-joe-black/
2. Chuck Klosterman. The Nineties: A Book
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 29.
In the first half of the 20th century Broadway musicals were a risky business. To save their productions, producers brought in patrons who would be nicknamed Charlies. Which word did we substitute in this question?

Answer: angels.
Comment: The patrons became like guardian angels for the productions. Several decades later the term came over into business, where investors who fund start-ups at early stages also came to be called angels. The substitution hints at the film title Charlie’s Angels.

Source: pureportal.strath.ac.uk/en/publications/business-angels
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 30.
This question used to contain 2 facts, but the author chose to keep only one. Maria Selvam, an activist, says that the Indian poor hope to visit the rich countries at least in a way. She means THIS. Identify THIS using exactly two words.

Answer: kidney transplantation [accepted answers: kidney transplant, kidney trade; same with another body parts].
Comment: These individuals have almost no chance to visit a rich country on their own, but they have an opportunity to improve their living standard by becoming an organ donor for money. Just like real donors, this question donated one of its facts to another question.

Source: Скотт Карни. Красный рынок. [Scott Carney. The Red Market.]
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 31.
The earliest newspapers focused on numerous ongoing wars, so they were often distributed together with THIS. One of the first examples of THIS has an image of a figure with its back bent beneath its burden. Identify THIS using exactly one word.

Answer: Atlas.
Comment: Readers had trouble finding their way through the many geographical names in the campaign descriptions, so a map collection came in handy. The word «atlas» for a map book was chosen after Atlas, the figure in Greek myth who held the skies on his shoulders.

Sources:
1. Эндрю Петтигри. Изобретение новостей. Как мир узнал о самом себе. [Andrew Pettegree. The Invention of News: How the World Came to Know About Itself]
2. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mercator_Hondius_Atlas_Minor_of_1607_frontispiece.png
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 32.
[Having read the answers out loud, read the acceptance criteria, given in italics.]
Attention! This is a double question. There will be 2 questions with 30 seconds’ thinking time for each. You must choose which of the two questions to answer. Answering both questions is not allowed.
1. In the times of racial segregation, the managers of one city utility enterprise in the state of Mississippi received a suggestion to prohibit sharing of THIS between white and black families. Identify THIS using exactly two words.
2. In the movie Pillow Talk, complaints about THIS draw characters closer to each other. Identify THIS using exactly two words.

Answer:
1. Shared line
2. Shared line
The answer card must have exactly one answer «shared line» (or equivalent, see below) to question 1 or question 2 of the double. If the phrase «shared line» (or equivalent) is written twice, the answer is not accepted.
[accepted answers: party line, shared telephone, party wire, multiparty line]
Comment: Shared lines, or party lines, were built in such a way that only one subscriber in the group could use the phone at any moment. The other subscriber(s) could eavesdrop on the call though, which was a frequent cause of complaints and arguments. And just like a shared line does not allow answering two calls simultaneously, in this double question you were only allowed to answer one of the two questions.

Sources:
1. https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=h_UlAAAAIBAJ&pg=820,5514413
2. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pillow_Talk_(film)
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 33.
The X in this question substitutes one word.
The comedian Milton Berle was sarcastic about the show business practices in the early years of the last century. In his routine he said that he laughed so hard at another comedian’s performance, that he almost dropped his X. In which country did an X falling down count as a positive result?

Answer: South Africa.
Comment: The X stands for «pencil». Milton Berle’s sarcasm was aimed at comedians stealing jokes. In South Africa, in the years of apartheid, a so-called «pencil test» was used to determine «racial purity». If a pencil didn’t get stuck in a person’s hair and fell down, the individual thus «tested» was counted as a white and their rights weren’t infringed.

Sources:
1. Lawrence J. Epstein. The Haunted Smile: The Story Of Jewish Comedians In America (https://clck.ru/32TUk5)
2. ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Карандашный_тест
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 34.
Maxim Gorky wrote that on weekends Americans go to amusement parks that poison their souls. Developing Gorky’s thought, John Kasson writes that for Americans THIS was actually amusement parks. Identify THIS using four words exactly.

Answer: opiate for the masses [accepted answers: opium/opiate of/for the people/masses, but only answers exactly matching this template].
Comment: According to Gorky, amusement parks were America’s substitute for religion, but like religion, they took workers’ attention away from class struggle. On his trip to the USA, Gorky spent a whole day on Coney Island rides and then wrote his scathing article.

Sources:
1. John F. Kasson. Amusing the million: Coney Island at the turn of the century
2. http://gorkiy-lit.ru/gorkiy/articles/article-367-2.htm
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 35.
Handout [

(img 2022-2023_III_en_001.jpeg)
]
In the USSR, extrasensory abilities were not believed to exist, until the emergence of news stories about Djuna the clairvoyant. As early as in the 80s, the poet Robert Rozhdestvensky [rozh-DEST-venn-ski] compared Djuna to THIS. Identify THIS using exactly two words.

Answer: black swan
Comment: The term «black swan» denotes an improbable development that suddenly becomes real. The term became popular much later than this, thanks to Nassim Taleb’s 2007 book, so this is most likely coincidental. Djuna’s dress on the picture might have reminded you of the black tutu in the movie Black Swan.

Sources:
1. https://djvu.online/file/CeDJ6aVULBbhN
2. ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Чёрный_лебедь_(теория)
Author: Alexei Sheredega

Question 36.
There are substituted words in this question. The scientist Paul Kammerer used to sit outside for days and write down how many people passed him by, how they were dressed, whether they met someone they knew. Kammerer wanted to prove that events are not fictitious. Which two words did we substitute in this question?

Answer: similarities, coincidental [accepted answers: for the first word, resemblances]
Comment: Kammerer was certain that all coincidences can be boiled down to specific laws and tried to formulate them empirically. The substitution is based on the usual disclaimer that all events depicted are fictitious and similarities are coincidental. We started the block with a question about coincidental roulette wins and finished with a question about coincidence.

Source: Джозеф Мазур. Игра случая. Математика и мифология совпадения [Joseph Mazur. Fluke: The Math and Myth of Coincidence]
Author: Alexei Sheredega
